name: Decap CMS
title: Mica vs. Decap CMS
summary: Both edit Git content for static websites. Decap CMS is a static admin app with an editorial workflow, languages and many Git providers. Mica is a local editor or a container you run, on a Git working tree, for Astro. Decap suits teams that want a static app and no service of their own.

chooseMica.text: You build with Astro and want an official package, with your content as typed Content Collections.
You want a local editor, or one container you run, with sign-in through your OpenID Connect provider.
Editors should see the real Astro page beside the form, with the drafts in it.
You want an editor to publish several changes as one commit, with a summary.
You want AI agents to save drafts through an MCP server that is built in and free.

chooseOther.text: You want an editorial workflow, with a pull request for each entry.
You need languages as a setting, with three file structures.
Your Git host is Bitbucket or Azure DevOps, or you want a wide choice of Git providers.
You want a preview pane from a React template of your own, updated as editors type.
You want a static app and no service to run, and a project with a large community.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Azure and Git Gateway. A local proxy edits local files.
Self-hosting: a static app under /admin. GitHub needs an OAuth server: Netlify, your own proxy, or Decap Turbo. GitLab and Gitea can use PKCE without a server. Hosted service: Decap Turbo.
None in the core. Decap Turbo, the hosted service, mirrors the repository into its own database.
MIT. Turbo on 21 October 2026: Free €0 (1 site, 1 seat), Pro €19 a month (1 site, 5 seats), Enterprise.
No official integration. The Astro documentation has a Decap guide. Content Collections read the files.
GitHub OAuth through a proxy, GitLab and Gitea PKCE, Bitbucket, Netlify Identity, Turbo accounts. Direct OIDC is not documented.
simple: each save commits. editorial_workflow: one branch and one pull request for each entry. It does not work with the local proxy. No batch publish documented.

A preview pane from a React template (registerPreviewTemplate), not the real site, updated as you type. Deploy preview links need the editorial workflow and a CI build per save. Click to edit on the page is not documented.
Not on GitHub (issue #1206 is open on 21 October 2026) and not on Gitea. GitLab reads LFS media since version 3.14.0.
Not supported. Issue #4056 is open on 21 October 2026.
The map widget stores a GeoJSON string. A stored zoom is not documented.
Not documented. Relations point to collections or to a file.
Not in the core (issue #2 is open on 21 October 2026). Turbo has roles as a paid add-on. Review goes through the editorial workflow.
Experimental. An MCP server and editor bridge in @decap/cli work with the paid Decap Turbo only.
